customer_jane: We're seeing intermittent 401s + latency spikes (3-6s) after we routed traffic through our on-prem proxy and created an interface endpoint in our AWS account. Started right after VPCE creation. Some requests return 200, many return 401. Any quick pointers?

sara_support: sorry about that — can you paste exact repro steps and a couple request IDs? Also confirm whether your proxy is doing TLS termination (SSL bump) or tunneling (CONNECT).

customer_jane: repro steps:
1) from onprem bastion -> curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
2) sometimes 200, often 401 with body 'invalid_token: aud mismatch'
3) latency ~3s on the ones that succeed and spikes to 5-6s on some failures

customer_jane: example output:
```
$ curl -v --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:10.10.5.21 https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci..."
* Connected to api.redwood.internal (10.10.5.21) port 443 (#0)
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
{ "error": "invalid_token", "error_description": "aud claim mismatch" }
```

alex_infra: thanks. Aud mismatch often happens when token aud is for the public hostname but the backend sees a different Host/SNI. Is your proxy terminating TLS and re-issuing requests? If so, SNI/Host might not match the token audience and our auth middleware rejects it.

mike_sre: also verify DNS from all subnets resolves to the VPCE interface IP and there's no hairpin NAT path. If the onprem proxy is doing SSL bump it may also be rewriting headers or altering the Authorization header.

sara_support: quick triage checks:
- curl from bastion to VPCE IP with the Host header and validate SNI with openssl:
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.21:443 -servername api.redwood.internal
```
Check certificate CN/SAN — should match our cert or the mapping you set up.

alex_infra: can you share a packet capture around TLS handshake? If SNI is missing the onprem proxy is terminating; if SNI present but Host header changed then the proxy is rewriting. Both are important clues.

customer_jane: confirmed: proxy currently terminates TLS and uses our corporate cert, then opens a new TLS connection to the VPCE. We tried whitelisting outbound IPs on our firewall but keep getting intermittent 401s. Our IdP issues tokens with aud=api.redwood.com (public). Should that be accepted by Redwood over the VPCE? We only changed DNS to point to VPCE.

mike_sre: Redwood can be audience-aware in some setups. If the proxy changes the Host the server sees, the aud check can fail. Two remediation paths:
1) configure the proxy to passthrough TLS (CONNECT) so SNI and original Host are preserved, OR
2) update your IdP to mint tokens with aud that matches the host seen by the VPCE (we can coordinate the exact host value).

sara_support: for latency: check proxy buffering and connection reuse. If the proxy creates new TLS for every request we see 2-4s added. Also check MTU/MSS on the appliance for PMTU blackhole causing large retransmission delays.

sara_support: immediate diagnostic commands to run from bastion (paste outputs here):
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:10.10.5.21 https://api.redwood.internal/health -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.21:443 -servername api.redwood.internal
tcpdump -A -s 0 -c 200 host 10.10.5.21 and port 443
```

customer_jane: attaching quick snippets below. Request IDs: r-01a2b3c4 r-01a2b3c5 r-01a2b3d0 (401s). We'll try switching the proxy to TLS passthrough in the next 30m. Can you enable extra auth logging on your side for a short window to help correlate?

sara_support: confirmed we see the three request IDs in our logs. Two were rejected with aud mismatch, one passed but had a 3.2s DB wait noted. We can enable extended auth debug logs for 1 hour if you approve — it will include token aud, Host, and SNI for every request to help correlation. Please confirm and we'll flip it on.

customer_jane: please enable the debug window. We'll switch to TLS passthrough and run tests, will paste results here.

deploy-bot: Created VPCE vpce-0a1b2c3d for svc/com.redwood/api in us-west-2 in account 987654321012 at 2026-03-17T14:00:01Z :white_check_mark:

alex_infra: follow-ups after your passthrough test: if auth issues are resolved but latency still high, check TCP MSS/MTU across the onprem appliance (PMTU), ensure keepalive/connection pooling from proxy to VPCE, and confirm there's no SNAT that changes source IP to one blocked by your VPCE policy.

mike_sre: we'll monitor once you run the passthrough test and collect the debug logs. Paste the tcpdump + curl outputs and we'll correlate with the request ids. :thumbsup:
